record.paper_title: FILTRATIONS BROWNIENNES ET COMPLÉMENTS INDÉPENDANTS : RÉSULTATS ET PROBLÈMES OUVERTS
record.context_brief: Open complementability question for the angular Brownian motion
record.original_question: Let Z = X + iY be a complex Brownian motion started from 0, let R_t = |Z_t|, define U_t = Z_t / R_t for t > 0, and define a new complex Brownian motion by Z'_t = ∫_0^t U_s dZ_s. Its imaginary part is the one-dimensional Brownian motion Y'_t = ∫_0^t (X_s dY_s − Y_s dX_s)/R_s. Is this Brownian motion Y' complementable in the natural filtration of (X, Y), meaning that there exists another one-dimensional Brownian motion in that filtration which is independent of Y' and together with Y' generates the same filtration as (X, Y)?

evidence.quote: Soit Z = X + iY un mouvement brownien complexe issu de 0. Notons S = X2 + Y2 et R = √S le module de Z. Presque sûrement t, le mouvement brownien Z ne repasse pas en 0, ce qui permet de poser Us = Zs / Rs pour s > 0 et de définir un nouveau mouvement brownien complexe Z0 par Z0t = R t 0 Us dZs. Les parties réelle et imaginaire de Z0 sont les mouvements browniens donnés par X0t = R t 0 XsdXs + YsdYs / Rs et Y0t = R t 0 XsdYs − YsdXs / Rs.

Comme la filtration naturelle de (X0, Y0) est strictement incluse dans celle de (X, Y), il est naturel de se demander si les mouvements browniens X0 et Y0 sont complémentables. Nous connaissons la réponse pour X0 mais pas pour Y0.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $Z=X+iY$ be a standard complex Brownian motion started from $0$, so that $X$ and $Y$ are independent real Brownian motions. Set $R_t=|Z_t|=\sqrt{X_t^2+Y_t^2}$, and, for $t>0$, $U_t=Z_t/R_t$ (well defined for almost every $t$ since planar Brownian motion almost surely does not return to $0$). Define a new complex Brownian motion $Z'$ by the Itô integral
$$Z'_t=\int_0^t U_s\,dZ_s,$$
and write $Z'=X'+iY'$, so that
$$X'_t=\int_0^t\frac{X_s\,dX_s+Y_s\,dY_s}{R_s},\qquad Y'_t=\int_0^t\frac{X_s\,dY_s-Y_s\,dX_s}{R_s}.$$
Then $Y'$ is a one-dimensional Brownian motion adapted to the natural filtration $\mathcal F^{(X,Y)}$ of the pair $(X,Y)$, and the natural filtration $\mathcal F^{Y'}$ of $Y'$ is strictly contained in $\mathcal F^{(X,Y)}$.

Say that a one-dimensional Brownian motion $B$ adapted to $\mathcal F^{(X,Y)}$ is complementable in $\mathcal F^{(X,Y)}$ if there exists another one-dimensional Brownian motion $C$ adapted to $\mathcal F^{(X,Y)}$ such that $B$ and $C$ are independent and the natural filtration of the pair $(B,C)$ equals $\mathcal F^{(X,Y)}$.

Question: Is the Brownian motion $Y'$ complementable in $\mathcal F^{(X,Y)}$?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears to have been resolved positively by Brossard, Émery and Leuridan in "Skew-Product Decomposition of Planar Brownian Motion and Complementability" (Séminaire de Probabilités XLVI, LNM 2123, 2014). They show that if $W$ is a complex Brownian motion whose natural filtration is the filtration of $Z$ up to an arbitrary rotation (which is exactly the case of $Z'$ above), then for every $a,b\in\mathbb R$ with $a^2+b^2=1$, the Brownian motion $a\,\Re(W)+b\,\Im(W)$ is complementable in $\mathcal F^Z$. Taking $a=0$, $b=1$ gives complementability of $Y'$.

status_evidence.title: Skew-Product Decomposition of Planar Brownian Motion and Complementability
status_evidence.snippet: For all a and b in R such that a²+b²=1, the Brownian motion aRe(W)+bIm(W) is complementable in F^Z.
status_evidence.claim: Brossard, Émery and Leuridan prove complementability of every linear combination of the real and imaginary parts of the skew-product Brownian motion W in F^Z, which yields complementability of Y'.

status_evidence.title: Complementability and maximality in different contexts (Leuridan)
status_evidence.snippet: Determining whether a 1-dimensional Brownian filtration immersed in a 2-dimensional Brownian filtration is complementable or not is often difficult; known cases are related to skew-product decomposition of the planar Brownian motion.
status_evidence.claim: The angular/skew-product case is among the known resolved complementability results.
